content: Interlanguage links are hyperlinks that connect a page in one language version of Wikipedia to the same subject in another language version of Wikipedia. These links also function between language versions of other Wikimedia projects, such as Wiktionary, Wikisource, Wikiquote, and Wikibooks. On Wikimedia Commons, interlanguage links provide connections to Wikipedia pages, but this is not reciprocal; links from Wikipedia to Commons are treated as in-page links. These links are typically displayed at the edges of a webpage, depending on the interface being used. For example, in the Monobook skin, they appear on the left side, while in the Classic skin, they are shown at the top and bottom of the page. They are listed under the section Other languages and display the names of the languages for which links are available. Although they resemble external links in appearance, their syntax is more similar to internal links. Interlanguage links are a specific type of interwiki link. The syntax for interlanguage links involves using a two-letter language code as defined by ISO 639-1. For instance, en represents English, de represents German, and so on. In an article like Plankton, which exists in multiple language versions, the interlanguage links would be formatted accordingly. These links are treated specially and do not appear in the main body of the text. Instead, they are displayed in a dedicated sidebar section labeled In other languages, sorted by language name. Previously, these links were placed at the top of the page, but this caused issues such as excessive whitespace, confusion for new editors, and irrelevant search results. As a result, it is now required to place them in the sidebar. The placement of interlanguage links within the article source does not affect their visual appearance on the rendered page, except for their order. However, it is important not to include a link to the language in which the article is written. Inline interlanguage links, which are clickable links within the text, can be created using a specific syntax. This is useful when a topic does not have its own page in the English Wikipedia but exists in another language version. For example, an article on Movie theaters in the Netherlands might include an inline link to the Dutch Wikipedia page for Tuschinski Theater if no English article exists yet. This approach encourages and facilitates the creation or translation of the article into English. In the past, the Chinese Wikipedia maintained separate versions of articles in Simplified and Traditional scripts. However, script conversion is now automated, eliminating the need for script-specific links. For other languages, there are lists of pages where interlanguage links may be needed. For example, an English article might have a link to a Spanish article, but the corresponding Spanish article might lack a link back to the English version. Lists of such pages are available for various languages, including Dutch, Esperanto, French, German, Polish, and Spanish. If you work on Wikipedia in multiple languages, it is helpful to monitor new pages in other languages and check for corresponding English articles to add links. When creating a link to another Wikipedia that also supports interlanguage links, it is recommended to create a reciprocal link in the other direction and copy any additional interlanguage links between the two pages. Inline interlanguage links are particularly useful for linking to topics that do not yet have a corresponding English article. For example, you might link Sigmund Freud to the German Wikipedia if no English article exists. These links can also be used for convenience on user pages to link to frequently visited pages or pages of interest to like-minded visitors. To create an inline interlanguage link, you can add a colon before the language abbreviation. For example, `[:fr:Littérature française au XVIIIe siècle]` would create a clickable link to the French Wikipedia article on 18th-century French literature. On talk pages and Meta, interlanguage links appear inline like regular links, allowing you to cite other pages in discussions. In normal articles, an inline link can be created by prefixing an extra colon, which is the recommended method for linking to an article in another language that is not the corresponding article. Interwiki links, which connect pages on different wikis, use a slightly different syntax from interlanguage links. For example, the prefix `en` can be used to link directly to the English Wikipedia, and `m` can be used for Meta-Wiki. These links are colored differently from internal links within the English Wikipedia and do not indicate whether the target page exists. If the target page does not exist, the link will lead to a blank page with no content, signaling that the article has not yet been written in the target language. Blank interlanguage links on the English Wikipedia can be deleted or commented out. It is strongly recommended to create at least a stub page before adding interlanguage links to it, as this allows others to translate the content into the new language. New articles should be sorted alphabetically based on the local language, as described in the interwiki sorting order guidelines. Sorting by the two-letter language abbreviations is also acceptable. Consistency in sorting methods across articles is encouraged. In cases where the interlanguage link feature is not available, or if you need to specify additional text in the link, you can use the regular external link syntax. This is useful when the subjects of the articles do not fully correspond.
